inputs.text: Well folks, let’s look at what we’ve got here. Decades of hard-left, socialist mismanagement have completely wrecked the foundation of community and family stability on the island, leaving ordinary residents owning nothing and struggling in poverty simply because socialist dogma stripped them of their autonomy and the fruits of their own labor. Now, the architects of this failure want to point fingers at free enterprise and property ownership as if the mere existence of outside capital is the original sin, while outside investors and a wealthy diaspora are swooping in to pick up the pieces, buying up property and businesses at bargain prices. They completely ignore the fact that it was decades of tyrannical state control that left these people structurally barred from success in the first place, destroying the natural social order and eradicating personal responsibility. If you actually want to protect working people, you have to restore respect for property, tradition, and self-reliance—instead of clinging to the hollow rhetoric of collective ownership that left everyone destitute to begin with.
